patches.title: [PATCH net v2 1/2] net: spacemit: Fix TX timeout work deadlocking on itself
patches.description: emac_tx_timeout_task(), the driver's TX-timeout recovery work, takes RTNL and calls dev_close(), which reaches emac_down(), which called cancel_work_sync() on that same work, so the work waited for itself with RTNL held. The fix removes that call: emac_suspend() and emac_remove() now cancel and disable the work with disable_work_sync(), emac_resume() re-enables it with enable_work(), and a normal close relies on the work's existing netif_running() check (the core clears the running state before calling .ndo_stop).
patches.impact: Every TX timeout on a SpacemiT K1 board, raised by the netdev watchdog when the TX queue has been stopped for more than 5 seconds, deadlocked the recovery work with RTNL held: the interface never came back, and every later operation that needs RTNL, such as interface, address and IPv4 route changes, blocked until reboot. Present since the driver was added in v6.18. With the fix, the work's close-and-reopen reset can complete. The change also removes a second deadlock, between an interface close and a TX-timeout work already waiting for RTNL.
patches.testing: Tested on Orange Pi RV2 (SpacemiT K1) with suspend/resume cycles and kselftest, with lockdep enabled. The deadlock was found by code inspection (reported by Troy Mitchell in review) and was not reproduced on hardware.

links.text: v1 review where the deadlock was reported

patches.title: [PATCH net v2 2/2] net: spacemit: Hold RTNL lock in emac_resume() and emac_suspend()
patches.description: emac_suspend() and emac_resume() called emac_stop() and emac_open(), the driver's .ndo_stop and .ndo_open, without RTNL, which the networking core always holds for those callbacks. On suspend, phy_disconnect() then read the RTNL-protected dev->hwprov pointer in phy_detach_internal() without the lock, and lockdep reported "suspicious RCU usage". Both callbacks now take RTNL before their netif_running() checks, so the interface cannot be opened or closed between the check and emac_stop() or emac_open(). Suspend disables the TX timeout work (patch 1/2) before taking the lock, so it never waits under RTNL for that work, which itself takes RTNL.
patches.impact: Suspend and resume on SpacemiT K1 boards now call .ndo_stop and .ndo_open under RTNL, as the networking core requires. The suspend warning, printed only by lockdep-enabled kernels (CONFIG_PROVE_RCU), is gone, and dev_open() or dev_close() can no longer run between the netif_running() check and the stop or open call.
patches.testing: Found by CI suspend tests on Orange Pi RV2 (SpacemiT K1). With lockdep: 12 suspend/resume cycles without the warning, no new kselftest failures. The board loses its network after about a dozen cycles with or without the series, a separate issue.

patches.title: [PATCH v3 1/2] PCI: plda: Fix use-after-free of event IRQs during teardown
patches.kernelVersion: v7.3 (backported to v6.12.109, v6.18.50, v7.2.4 stable)

cve.headline: Use-after-free in PLDA PCIe host IRQ teardown
cve.importance: Use-after-free of the event IRQ domain in StarFive JH7110 PCIe teardown, reachable only via privileged driver unbind or module unload, or a host-bridge registration failure during probe.

patches.description: Fixed a use-after-free in the shared PLDA PCIe host teardown path. plda_pcie_irq_domain_deinit() removed the event IRQ domain with irq_domain_remove(), but the per-event IRQs mapped from that domain are requested with devm_request_irq(), so their free_irq() is deferred by devres until after a failed probe() or remove() returns, and then dereferences the already-freed domain while deactivating the interrupt. Each event IRQ is now released explicitly with devm_free_irq() before the domain goes away, the event-domain mappings (including the INTx and MSI summary IRQs) are disposed of with irq_dispose_mapping(), and the chained-handler teardown is guarded so it only runs for valid IRQ numbers.
patches.impact: Removes a use-after-free that affected StarFive JH7110, the only in-tree user of the PLDA host init/deinit helpers (Microchip PolarFire SoC never calls them). Also stops event IRQ mappings from leaking and prepares plda_pcie_irq_domain_deinit() for the error-path unwinding added in patch 2/2.
patches.testing: Build-tested and boot-tested on StarFive VisionFive 2 v1.2A.

patches.title: [PATCH v3 2/2] PCI: plda: Fix IRQ domain leaks in the error paths of plda_init_interrupts()
patches.kernelVersion: v7.3 (backported to v6.12.109, v6.18.50, v7.2.4 stable)

cve.headline: IRQ domain leak in PLDA PCIe host error paths
cve.importance: Permanent leak of IRQ domains and mappings in StarFive JH7110 and Microchip PolarFire SoC PCIe probe, reachable only when interrupt setup fails after domain creation, e.g. a bad device-tree interrupt.

patches.description: plda_init_interrupts() created IRQ domains and IRQ mappings but returned without unwinding them when a later step failed, and neither in-tree caller tore them down. A failing platform_get_irq(), irq_create_mapping() or event IRQ request left the domains allocated, and a failed MSI mapping also left port->intx_irq mapped. Every error path after domain creation now jumps to one label that calls plda_pcie_irq_domain_deinit(), which, since companion patch 1/2, also disposes of the event-domain mappings, including the INTx and MSI summary IRQs.
patches.impact: Interrupt-setup failures now unwind through the same plda_pcie_irq_domain_deinit() already used on host-bridge registration failure and StarFive driver removal, which is why this patch depends on patch 1/2; a probe that fails after IRQ domain creation on either in-tree host no longer leaves IRQ domains and IRQ descriptors behind.
patches.testing: Build-tested and boot-tested on StarFive VisionFive 2 v1.2A together with patch 1/2.

patches.title: [PATCH v3] PCI: starfive: Fix resource leaks on error paths in host_init()
patches.kernelVersion: v7.3 (backported to v6.12.112, v6.18.51, v7.2.4 stable)
patches.description: Fixed two error paths in starfive_pcie_host_init() for the StarFive JH7110 PCIe controller. When starfive_pcie_clk_rst_init() failed, the function returned without disabling the already-enabled PHY, leaving it powered on. A regulator_enable() failure on the optional vpcie3v3 slot supply was only logged and success was returned, so the driver kept configuring PCIe hardware that might be unpowered. Both paths now unwind in reverse order and return the error.
patches.impact: A vpcie3v3 enable failure now fails probe with its error code; previously the error was swallowed and bring-up continued with the slot possibly unpowered, and any later teardown triggered an unbalanced regulator_disable() warning. A clock/reset failure no longer leaves the PHY powered on.
patches.testing: Build-tested and boot-tested on StarFive VisionFive 2 v1.2A.

patches.title: [PATCH v2] PCI: starfive: Fix Runtime PM handling and teardown ordering
patches.kernelVersion: v7.3 (backported to v6.12.110, v6.18.52, v7.2.6 stable)
patches.description: starfive_pcie_remove() dropped the runtime PM reference and disabled runtime PM before calling plda_pcie_host_deinit(), so teardown did not mirror probe, which takes that reference before plda_pcie_host_init(). Removal now deinitializes the host first, while the reference is still held, and only then calls pm_runtime_put_sync() and pm_runtime_disable(), the same sequence as the probe error path. The put is synchronous because an asynchronous pm_runtime_put() followed immediately by pm_runtime_disable() can cancel the still-queued idle request and leave the device marked active.
patches.impact: Driver unbind and module unload now tear down the host in reverse probe order, and the device is runtime-suspended before runtime PM is disabled. A latent ordering bug found by automated review: on JH7110, runtime PM gates no clock or power domain, so it had caused no observed failure.

patches.title: [PATCH v2] PCI: starfive: Fix unchecked pm_runtime_get_sync() in probe
patches.kernelVersion: v7.3 (backported to v6.12.110, v6.18.52, v7.2.6 stable)
patches.description: starfive_pcie_probe() called pm_runtime_get_sync() without checking its return value, so a failed runtime resume still let probe continue into starfive_pcie_host_init(), which powers on the PHY, programs the STG syscon through regmap_update_bits(), and enables clocks and deasserts resets on a device that may not have been powered. Because pm_runtime_get_sync() keeps the usage counter incremented on failure, the probe now uses pm_runtime_resume_and_get(), which drops the reference itself on failure, and on error disables runtime PM and returns through dev_err_probe() before plda_pcie_host_init() touches the controller.
patches.impact: A failed runtime resume now fails probe before the PHY, syscon, clocks or controller registers are touched, with runtime PM unwound. Error-path hardening: the driver has no runtime PM callbacks and the in-tree JH7110 PCIe nodes have no power domain, so the path is not normally reached.
patches.testing: Tested on StarFive VisionFive 2 v1.2A board.

patches.title: [PATCH] wifi: rtl8xxxu: fix slab-out-of-bounds in rtl8xxxu_sta_add
patches.kernelVersion: v7.0 (backported to v6.12.72, v6.18.11, v6.19.1 stable)

cve.headline: Heap out-of-bounds write in the rtl8xxxu Wi-Fi driver
cve.importance: Heap out-of-bounds write whenever an rtl8xxxu adapter associates or accepts a client, reachable in AP mode by unauthenticated nearby devices; rated HIGH by the kernel CNA (8.8) and NVD (7.8).

patches.description: Fixed a slab-out-of-bounds write in the rtl8xxxu USB Wi-Fi driver. The driver never set hw->sta_data_size, so mac80211's __sta_info_alloc() allocated no space for the per-station private area, and rtl8xxxu_sta_add() wrote struct rtl8xxxu_sta_info fields through sta->drv_priv past the end of the allocation. The fix sets hw->sta_data_size to sizeof(struct rtl8xxxu_sta_info) in rtl8xxxu_probe(). Caught by KASAN on RISC-V with an RTL8192EU adapter.
patches.impact: The out-of-bounds accesses did not stop at rtl8xxxu_sta_add(): RX RSSI averaging (ewma_rssi_add()), the 2-second rate-adaptation watchdog and TX descriptor setup kept using the same out-of-bounds region for as long as the station stayed associated.
patches.testing: Tested with RTL8192EU adapter on StarFive VisionFive 2 (RISC-V). Verified with KASAN enabled that the slab-out-of-bounds write is eliminated.

patches.title: [PATCH] spi: cadence-qspi: Fix runtime PM imbalance in probe
patches.description: Fixed a runtime PM usage count underflow in the Cadence Quad SPI controller driver. Commit 30dbc1c8d50f made the success path of cqspi_probe() call pm_runtime_put_autosuspend() twice while only one reference was taken with pm_runtime_get_noresume(); the patch removes the first, redundant call.
patches.impact: Fixes the "Runtime PM usage count underflow!" warning that 30dbc1c8d50f (v6.17) caused at probe on every platform except SoCFPGA, where the driver disables runtime PM; the PM core rejected the extra put, so the warning was the only visible effect. The same one-line fix by another contributor (10eaa4c4a257) reached mainline first, in v6.18, so this commit duplicated it when the SPI tree was merged for v6.19.
patches.testing: Verified on StarFive VisionFive 2 v1.2A that the runtime PM warning no longer appears during boot and driver probe.

patches.title: [PATCH v3] pinctrl: starfive: use dynamic GPIO base allocation
patches.description: Switched the StarFive JH7110 (RISC-V SoC) pinctrl driver from the deprecated static GPIO base to dynamic allocation by setting sfp->gc.base = -1 in jh7110_pinctrl_probe(). Removed the now-unused gc_base member of struct jh7110_pinctrl_soc_info and the JH7110_SYS_GC_BASE (0) and JH7110_AON_GC_BASE (64) constants of the sys and aon controllers.
patches.impact: Removes the warning "Static allocation of GPIO base is deprecated, use dynamic allocation." that the GPIO core printed at probe for both JH7110 GPIO controllers (fixed bases 0 and 64) since the driver was added in v6.3. Their bases now come from the dynamic range starting at 512, so GPIO numbers in the deprecated global sysfs interface change; device-tree consumers and /dev/gpiochipN users address lines by chip offset and are unaffected.
patches.testing: Tested on StarFive VisionFive 2. Verified GPIO functionality remains correct with dynamic allocation. Confirmed no deprecation warnings during boot.
